source.title: Aug-NeRF: Training Stronger Neural Radiance Fields with Triple-Level Physically-Grounded Augmentations
source.authors: Tian-Long Chen; Pei-Hao Wang; Zhi-Wen Fan; Zhang-Yang Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper, including the appendix; some PDF layout and table text are flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results that refine when augmentation changes NeRF’s train-to-test behavior, including less benefit from random perturbations, sensitivity to augmentation strength and location, and results across model-size and data-scale settings. It does not test the claim’s random-label memorization or classifier generalization versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies novel-view synthesis by NeRF and Aug-NeRF, not fitting arbitrary labels or classification error relative to chance. Rows record its reported held-out-view metrics and ablations relevant to generalization, plus its explicit regularization comparators and the model-size/data-scale comparison. Reported settings used only to select hyperparameters are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a presumed connection between flat loss landscapes and generalization to motivate Aug-NeRF, then evaluates its synthesis and reconstruction performance. It does not test any listed version. Feature or coordinate perturbations do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled weight sharpness; the width comparisons do not establish V2's zero-training-error threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase correctly describes improved geometry continuity, novel-view synthesis and noisy-supervision tolerance as a by-product. Its corruption-scope statement needs qualification: although the conclusion says only additive noise was studied, Appendix A2/Table A6 also reports pepper noise and inaccurate camera poses. Inaccurate-pose results improve PSNR, SSIM and Average, but worsen LPIPS from 0.725 to 0.811.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses NeRF-style training with adversarial augmentation at input coordinates, intermediate features, and pre-rendering outputs. It evaluates novel-view synthesis and geometry, rather than arbitrary-label fitting and classification generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that augmentation gains depend on perturbation strength and injection location; too-strong perturbations such as PGD-10 may deteriorate performance, and the middle MLP layer contributes most among tested feature injection positions. Hyperparameter settings are described as grid-search choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Aug-NeRF improves held-out synthesis metrics over vanilla NeRF across six evaluated scenes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Triple-level adversarial augmentation improves NeRF novel-view synthesis in the evaluated scenes.

fits_no_version.finding: Aug-NeRF improves all reported synthesis metrics under Gaussian and shot-noise supervision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aug-NeRF improves novel-view synthesis from Gaussian- or shot-corrupted fern training images.

fits_no_version.finding: Augmentation levels contribute differently; random perturbations provide smaller gains than the complete adversarial method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NeRF synthesis gains depend on augmentation location and perturbation construction.

fits_no_version.finding: Density sparsity and Laplacian regularization worsen average synthesis error; TV improves it less than Aug-NeRF.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit density regularizers differ in their effects on NeRF held-out synthesis quality.

fits_no_version.finding: Aug-NeRF improves synthesis metrics within each tested width/resolution combination.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aug-NeRF benefits the three tested chair model-size and image-resolution settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Chair geometry Chamfer Distance falls from 0.0147 to 0.0104.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aug-NeRF improves chair geometry reconstruction in the reported evaluation.

record.peer_reviewed: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (as stated in supplied metadata)
record.problems: The evaluation covers six representative scenes and reports no uncertainty estimates. The supplied Table 2 layout is partly flattened, preventing confident recovery of some NeRF baseline values and metric pairings. The reported test-view metrics do not provide train error or a train-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Hyperparameter sweeps in Figure 7 are not individually transcribed because their plotted values are figure-only and the text identifies them as configuration choices; the text-described strength and location sensitivity is retained in method_sensitivity.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and matched natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight sharpness, its correlation with measured generalization gaps, and comparison with norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain unlinked to the listed versions. Missing training error is decisive for V2's interpolation condition and V7's gap analysis, but is not a universal requirement for every version. Table A6 supplies additional out-of-version results, so it does not require a version-linked missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error as width increases.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and held-out classification or language performance.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
